newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to mostly $0.50 per cwt lower amid ongoing light demand from packers with unprofitable operating margins, livestock dealers said.
Top prices for interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs delivered to the plant could range $52.50 to $53.00 and top prices in Illinois could range $52.00 to $52.50.
Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs at the plant could range $52.00 to $52.50, possibly $53.00.
Although prices were seen mostly lower, tighter hog supplies could put a bottom in the market, dealers said.

Soft pork demand has eroded packer operating margins, resulting in minimum operating hours, the dealers said. At least one major packer dropped indefinitely the second shift at one of its two large hog plants as of last Monday.
Fresh pork prices were steady to lower at midday in light activity, USDA said.

There was a weak undertone noted for loins, steady-firm undertone for butts and steady for hams, USDA said. Bellies were not tested and lean trimmings were $1.00 to $3.00 lower. There were 36.0 loads of pork cuts and 3.0 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold.
